## Purpose and Entry Points
`kubectl-ai` is a Go CLI/kubectl plugin that turns natural-language requests into Kubernetes operations through an LLM agent. Primary startup paths are the normal CLI in `cmd/main.go` and MCP-server mode in `cmd/mcp.go`. It accepts interactive terminal input, piped/one-shot prompts, or an HTML UI.

## Application Composition
The agent is assembled around conversation state, an LLM client, tools, UI, and optional persistence. `pkg/agent/manager.go` coordinates request execution; `pkg/agent/conversation.go` maintains multi-turn context; `pkg/api/models.go` supplies shared API models. The agent iterates up to configured limits, letting model tool calls drive execution and returning streamed/final output to the UI.

## LLM Provider Boundary
The nested `gollm` Go module abstracts model-specific APIs behind common interfaces and a provider factory: `gollm/interfaces.go`, `gollm/factory.go`, `gollm/schema.go`. Implementations support Gemini, OpenAI-compatible/Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Grok, Bedrock, Ollama, and llama.cpp, separating provider authentication/protocols from agent orchestration. Journal/persistence facilities support recording and replayable LLM HTTP/context data in `gollm/http_journal.go` and `gollm/persist.go`.

## Tool Execution and Kubernetes Safety Boundary
Tools exposed to the model are defined and assembled in `pkg/tools/interfaces.go`, `pkg/tools/tools.go`, and `pkg/tools/kubectl_tool.go`. Built-ins include kubectl and bash; YAML-defined custom tools and MCP-backed tools extend the same tool surface. Kubernetes commands can be filtered and routed through permission/sandbox controls, with execution backends in `pkg/sandbox/executor.go`, `pkg/sandbox/kubernetes.go`, and `pkg/sandbox/local.go`. This is the critical boundary between generated model instructions and cluster/local side effects.

## MCP Integration Hub
In client mode, configured external MCP servers are discovered and translated into callable tools via `pkg/mcp/manager.go`, `pkg/mcp/stdio_client.go`, and `pkg/mcp/http_client.go`; the agent consumes them through `pkg/agent/mcp_client.go` and `pkg/tools/mcp_tool.go`. In server mode, `cmd/mcp.go` exposes native tools, optionally aggregates those external tools, and supports stdio or streamable HTTP transport. This makes the binary both an MCP tool consumer and provider.

## State, Interaction, and Observability
Session storage is abstracted by `pkg/sessions/store.go` and managed through `pkg/sessions/manager.go`, with memory and filesystem implementations in `pkg/sessions/memory.go` and `pkg/sessions/filesystem.go`. UI adapters in `pkg/ui/terminal.go`, `pkg/ui/tui.go`, and `pkg/ui/html/htmlui.go` present the same agent flow through terminal, TUI, or web runtime. Execution/context logging is handled by `pkg/journal/recorder.go` and `pkg/journal/loader.go`.

## Deployment and External Dependencies
The runtime needs a configured kubeconfig/kubectl and credentials for the selected LLM provider. Container packaging is `images/kubectl-ai/Dockerfile`; Kubernetes deployment manifests are `k8s/kubectl-ai.yaml` and `k8s/kubectl-ai-gke.yaml`. Local or cluster-hosted llama.cpp serving is supplied separately under `modelserving/k8s/llm-server.yaml` and `modelserving/images/llamacpp-server/Dockerfile`. Releases are built through GoReleaser (`.goreleaser.yaml`) and distributed as a standalone binary/Krew plugin.
